claims.text: Machine-learning-guided optimization of thermomechanical processing will produce a hierarchical microstructure containing fine, uniformly distributed, coherent precipitates in high-entropy alloys.
The resulting microstructure will simultaneously improve strength, ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance relative to conventional processing.
Conventionally cast or heat-treated high-entropy alloys have relatively coarse microstructures and suboptimal precipitate distributions.
Conventional processing commonly produces a strength–ductility trade-off.
A data-driven model can identify optimal temperature profiles, strain rates, and annealing durations for the targeted high-entropy alloy.
High-pressure/high-temperature treatment or spark plasma sintering can tailor and refine high-entropy-alloy microstructures.
The intervention should work when compositions and processing parameters remain within the machine-learning model’s training or predictive domain.
The intervention may fail for compositions substantially different from the training data or under extreme thermal gradients or cooling rates.
Optimized processing alters nucleation and growth kinetics, refines grains, and promotes coherent precipitate formation.
The refined microstructure minimizes dislocation pile-ups and reduces interfacial stress concentrations.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups and interfacial stress concentrations breaks the strength–ductility trade-off.
The proposed microstructural evolution will modestly increase stiffness and improve fracture resistance.
Machine-learning-guided processing will increase tensile yield strength by more than 10% relative to the conventionally processed baseline.
Machine-learning-guided processing will increase elongation to failure relative to the baseline.
Machine-learning-guided processing will slightly increase Young’s modulus relative to the baseline.
Machine-learning-guided processing will increase energy absorption or crack-growth resistance relative to the baseline.

Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering can control phase evolution and microstructure refinement while producing high hardness and compressive strength in CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy.
Unmodeled alloying-element interactions may confound the expected property improvements.

contradictions.description: The intervention explicitly includes high-pressure/high-temperature treatment, whereas the stated operating conditions describe processing at ambient to only moderately elevated temperatures.
